units.translation: where φάει [in light] is inappropriate, but déeι is fitting, which Auratus conjectured. The scholiast seems to have read φάει καρδίας [in the light of the heart], who explains it as λαμπρότητι, ὀρθότητι φρενών [by the brightness, uprightness of mind]. After καρδίαν [heart] one syllable has fallen out, unless the poet opposed an unresolved form to the tribrach which is read in the strophic verse 516 ἢ τεκοῦσα νεοπαθής [or having borne a new grief]: whence Hermann conjectured ἔτ᾽ ἀνατρέφων [still nurturing].
